title: Ayni Agent pack (schema 3.0)
description: Single configuration bundle of a Ayni Agent: behavior and policy (spec CORE-PACK-001). Any string value may contain ${VAR} or ${VAR:-default} placeholders resolved from the environment at load time (CORE-PACK-002).

schemaVersion.description: Agent-pack schema version (CORE-PACK-004). Major must be 3.

id.description: Stable agent identifier (used in logs, statistics, object keys).

displayName.description: Name shown in the descriptor, menus and binding questions. Must match the ECS-Service credential name once trust resolution confirms it.

identity.description: Who this agent is and how it turns verified facts into roles (D30, D31, D34, D37, D38).

homeBackingIdentity.description: DID of this agent, the Verifiable Service its operator runs (D30, D37). The organization of its own ECS Organization credential is the home organization, and no other is (D64, IDENT-ROLE-011).

userAgentGate.description: Whether a connecting user agent must present an ECS-UserAgent credential (D38, IDENT-RES-003).

authentication.description: How a person authenticates (D125, IDENT-AUTH-001, IDENT-RES-010): the methods enabled, keyed by a name the operator chooses, and the accepted combinations of them, one of which the person completes on the phone in one authenticate flow (D128). Omitted, or with no combination, by an agent that authenticates nobody: everyone then enters unidentified (D53).

request.description: When it is asked: on-connect (default), before any conversation; on-demand, only when it is asked for, by the person, from their wallet or a menu item, or by the model's tool, the person entering as a visitor meanwhile (D53, D65, D72).

visitors.description: Whether a person may enter without authenticating, as a visitor (D72). With on-connect: false (default), the authentication is required and nothing opens without it; true, it is offered at connection and the person may continue as a visitor. on-demand lets visitors in by itself and refuses false.

methods.description: The methods enabled, by name (D126): credential (a presentation of a credential of a schema), email (a code sent to an address of the user directory), document (the chip of a passport or identity card, matched to an entry of the directory), face-match (a live face against a reference picture; confirms), authenticator-app (a TOTP code; confirms; enrolled on the phone), passkey (enrolled on the phone).

type.description: credential, email, document, face-match, authenticator-app or passkey; another type stops the start, naming the method (IDENT-AUTH-001).

credential.description: A credential method: its schema, asked by its ecosystem schema so that any accredited issuer satisfies the request.

subjectKey.description: A credential method: the attributes that, with the organization of the issuer and the schema, form the principal key of a person of another organization (D59): badgeNumber for the ECS-Badge.

attributes.description: A credential method: the attributes asked of the credential; every attribute of the schema when omitted.

issuers.description: A credential method: whose credentials are accepted (D72). Absent: any accredited issuer of the schema that an organization backs.

organizations.description: The organization keys accepted: org:<country>:<register id>, as the verified Organization credential of the issuer gives them.

reference.description: A face-match method: the reference picture, in order of preference (D131): document, the portrait of a passport read in the same authentication; directory, the photo of the entry found.

combinations.description: The accepted combinations, each a list of method names: the person is identified once every method of one of them completed in one authenticate flow (D125, D127). Each holds an identifying method (credential, email, document, passkey).

obtain.description: How a person obtains what they lack to authenticate (a credential, an address the agent knows), in the operator's words, with a link when there is one (D72). Shown by the phone to a person who can complete no combination, or whose authentication was not accepted.

organization.description: The home organization's own words about itself (D123): the domains of its people's email addresses. An address of another domain is outside the organization, which makes a call that names it external (TOOL-FEAT-013); with no list, every address is outside.

organizations.description: Patterns over the verified attributes of an organization's ECS Organization credential, evaluated in order, first match wins; no match is unrecognized (D64, IDENT-ROLE-008). A pattern never sets home: home is the agent's own organization only (IDENT-ROLE-011).

roleRules.description: Evaluated in order over verified facts; the first matching rule assigns the roles (D34). No match: authenticated, no backing identity, public-only.

userAgentVerified.description: Match on whether the ECS-UserAgent credential was presented (only meaningful with userAgentGate optional).

claims.description: Verified claim values that must all match (ECS-Badge facts such as department or title, or ECS-Service attributes). A list matches any of its values.

perActorOverrides.description: Roles for specific known actors, applied before roleRules (D34).

actor.description: ECS-Service id of a service, or the ECS-Badge subject identifier of a person.

directory.description: The user directory (D79, D87, IDENT-ROLE-012): the people of the home organization, their department, groups and roles typed by hand, in a file mounted from a secret of the deployment. The people are never written in the agent-pack: a pack that lists them is refused. A relative path resolves from the pack directory. The agent reloads the file when it changes (IDENT-ROLE-013).

file.description: Path of the directory file: YAML or JSON holding a list `people`.

roles.description: Declared roles with the approval rights they carry (RBAC-TOOL, INTX-APPR). Any role named in roleRules, toolAccess or approvers must be declared here.

canApprove.description: May act as an approver where listed.

admin.description: The role reads the admin view of the user directory: who holds which role and why, and what each reload changed (IDENT-DIR-008/009, PROF-DIR-003). A role carries no scope of conversation reads (RBAC-XSESS-005).

credentials.description: Other credentials the agent requests on DIDComm connect (IDENT-RES-001/003). userAgent: the ECS-UserAgent credential of the Verifiable User Agent gate; service: credentials accepted from a verifiable-service peer. The credential that authenticates a person is identity.authentication.

language.description: One agent language (D21). Presentation language is the channel's or frontend's concern.

persona.description: The author's prompt and interaction surface (D46). The platform appends its own system-prompt add-on; the persona never overrides it (CORE-PROMPT-001).

greeting.description: Sent on first contact and on each new conversation; {userName} is replaced by the Principal's display name.

menu.description: Contextual menu items (INTX-MENU). Built-in commands (sessions, approvals) are added by the platform and need no entry.

type.description: prompt: send a text as the user's turn; tool: call a tool directly if allowed; url: open a link.

roles.description: With visibleWhen role: roles that see the item.

llm.description: Language model provider and model (LLM-PROV). Keys come from the environment, never from the pack.

provider.description: Adapter: native (openai, anthropic, ollama), generic chat-completions (openai-compatible), special-protocol (azure-openai, bedrock, vertex). stub is a deterministic offline model for development and tests only.

providerName.description: The name of the model provider the allowedProviders of spaces list, such as kimi for openai-compatible on Moonshot (ayni-agent decision 60); provider when absent.

baseUrl.description: Endpoint base URL. Required for ollama and openai-compatible (gateways included); the LLM_BASE_URL variable supplies it when absent.

apiKeyEnv.description: Name of the environment variable holding the key.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. Omit it for endpoints that do not accept the parameter (for example Kimi K3).

reasoningEffort.description: Passed as reasoning_effort to providers that accept it (OpenAI reasoning models; Kimi K3 accepts low, high, max).

multimodal.description: Pass referenced media to the model when it supports it (LLM-MODE-002). Never required.

provider_options.description: Provider-specific settings as the adapter documents (deployment name, region, project).

maxInputTokens.description: The model's input limit (MEM-CTX-006). The agent refuses to start when memory.contextWindowTokens plus maxOutputTokens exceeds it.

cache.description: Provider caching by prefix (LLM-CACHE-001): the conversation is sent as the cache key, with the lifetime below. Kimi (openai-compatible) first.

embeddings.description: Embeddings provider for the semantic index and RAG (LLM-EMB). Independent of llm.

provider.description: stub is an offline hash embedding for development and tests only.

memory.description: Memory tiers and retrieval (D9, D10, D24, D25).

contextWindowTokens.description: Token budget of the context window (MEM-RET-001, MEM-CTX-002); CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS sets it in the Welcome pack.

keepRatio.description: A step drops the oldest entries until the context fits this share of the budget.

maxEntries.description: The number of entries the window reads; a step also drops the entries beyond it.

summarization.description: The conversation summary (MEM-CTX-004): the entries a step drops, compressed with the previous summary.

triggerTokens.description: The window steps when the context would exceed this many tokens; defaults to contextWindowTokens.

maxSummaryTokens.description: The output limit of a summary.

ambientDescriptions.description: Keep short stored descriptions of recent entries in context (D24).

rag.description: Corpus sources exposed to the LLM as a tool (D42, MEM-RAG). Each source carries a visibility (MEM-RAG-005).

path.description: Directory or file for local sources.

partner.description: The organization key of the partner (org:<country>:<registry id>) whose Principals may read a partner-shared source (MEM-RAG-005).

presentations.description: The credentials the agent may ask for, beyond the one that authenticates (D69, INTX-PRES-001): a closed list by name. What comes back is evidence attached to the Principal of the connection; it never binds one.

subjectKind.description: To whom credentials of the schema are issued; the entry is asked of such a peer only (INTX-PRES-007). Declared here under Verifiable Trust v4.

request.description: on-connect: asked by the code when the connection is established; on-demand: asked when the model names the entry with request_presentation.

purpose.description: Why the credential is asked, shown before the answer (INTX-PRES-008).

attributes.description: The attributes asked of the credential; every attribute of the schema when omitted.

evidence.description: The evidence that is not a credential (D73, D89, PRIV-EVID-003): what is kept of a document read (the document challenge) and of an address verified by an email code (the email challenge of a badge from the directory), and what the model may read of it. The attributes of a document read are a closed list: documentType, documentNumber, issuingState, nationality, lastName, firstName, fullName, dateOfBirth, dateOfExpiry, sex, portrait. An email check has one: address, which the model never reads.

email.description: What is kept of an address an email method verified (IDENT-AUTH-009): its one attribute is address. A profile that takes a claim from a verified address (emailId) needs it stored; the model never reads it, so modelVisible is refused.

issuance.description: The credentials the agent may issue: a closed list by name, each claim with one source that is never the model (D70, INTX-ISSUE-001).

credential.description: The credential issued, named by a credential definition of this agent or by the schema of the credential in its ecosystem: the agent then uses the definition its DIDComm agent holds for that schema and creates it when there is none (INTX-ISSUE-017).

label.description: How the credential is named to a person, in the menu.

subjectKind.description: To whom credentials of the schema are issued. Persons only in this version.

trigger.description: Who starts the issuance (INTX-ISSUE-008): model, the LLM with issue_credential; request, the person from a menu item; automatic, the agent as soon as every claim resolves.

authChallenge.description: The challenge enforced before the issuance (INTX-ISSUE-010): one, written alone or as a list of one. A badge from the user directory needs none: its claims come from the entry the authentication identified (D130).

evidenceMaxAgeMinutes.description: Evidence older than this is expired for the profile (INTX-ISSUE-013).

validUntilClaim.description: The claim that holds the last day the credential is valid, a date: the issuance record keeps it, and a credential past it is held no more, so that an automatic profile is offered again on the connection (IDENT-AUTH-016, INTX-ISSUE-023). Without it the credential holds until it is revoked.

claims.description: Every claim of the credential with its one source (INTX-ISSUE-002). evidence: a stored attribute of the authentication, of a presentations entry, of a document read or of a verified email, `as: dateint` writing a calendar date as the integer YYYYMMDD (IDENT-DIR-005); record: a field of the person's entry of the user directory, found from their evidence (INTX-ISSUE-021); computed: today, now, addDays (days), constant (value), subjectId, documentId or emailId.

record.description: What is kept of an issuance beyond its audit fields (INTX-ISSUE-014).

tools.description: The tool catalog (D96, D101, D120, TOOL-CAT, TOOL-FEAT): the features, in the words people use, and the sources, one map keyed by the source id, each MCP server or HTTP tool naming the feature it serves. mcp.servers, tools.http, tools.bundled, tools.access and actions are withdrawn and refused at start (TOOL-CAT-011).

features.description: The features (D120, TOOL-FEAT-001), keyed by the feature's id. A feature with profile has a contract, a feature profile the agent knows (org.ayni/files 1.0, org.ayni/calendar 1.0), whose tools every provider gives the model; one without is a category, its provider's own tools shown under its title.

purposes.description: The governance list a principal may declare when requesting elevation (D14, D15, PRIV-ELEV).

permittedRoles.description: Optional restriction: only these roles may declare this purpose (D15).

approvals.description: Defaults for approval and elevation policies (INTX-APPR). Per-tool entries in toolAccess may override them.

selfApproval.description: A requester who holds an approver role for the tool runs it without a prompt (INTX-APPR).

grantTtlMinutes.description: Default duration of an elevation grant.

approvers.description: The roles that approve a tool of the whole agent or of Personal whose rule is approval and that no toolAccess.approval entry lists (TOOL-CAT-009).

timeoutSeconds.description: How long a confirmation card waits (TOOL-CALL-004).

spaces.description: The approval policies of the tools of spaces (TOOL-CAT-023, D140): the default a tool takes until the owner sets one, the bounds the owner works within, and the timeouts of a space per kind of approval (SPACE-DEF-008).

sessions.description: Session lifecycle (D6, D7, D36). Deployment-tunable through ${VAR} placeholders.

siblingSessions.description: Allow sibling sessions from a bound token (CHAN-BIND-010).

devicePairing.description: Device pairing (D51, IDENT-DEV-004): a browser the phone confirmed once binds later sessions without the phone while the pairing is used within slidingDays and younger than maxDays. slidingDays 0 disables silent binding.

channels.description: Channel adapters (D1, D2). DIDComm is always on: it is the capability channel.

allowedOrigins.description: UI origins allowed by CORS on the session endpoints.

walletLinkTemplate.description: HTTPS app link with {oob}; never a didcomm:// link (PROF-BIND-008).

appLinkBase.description: Base of the app links the model may write in replies, on the network's app-link domain (AG-UI profile section 10, PROF-LINK-001); absent: the model writes no app links.

privacy.description: Processing activities with lawful basis and retention (D18, PRIV-RETN), erasure settings (D19, D20).

onExpiry.description: Histories are archived, never deleted, so the digest chain stays verifiable (PRIV-RETN-002).

erasureRequests.description: Accept erasure requests (crypto-erasure with lineage cascade).

media.description: Inbound media to text and media generation (D45).

provider.description: llm reuses the configured language model when it is multimodal.

faceVerification.description: Face-match challenges (INTX-AUTH-007/008): a call on the capability channel joined by the face-verification service.

features.description: Feature gates. A disabled feature is absent from the system-prompt add-on (CORE-PROMPT-002) and from the descriptor.

conversations.description: What a person may do with their conversations (ayni-agent decision 60).

messageDeletionWindowSeconds.description: A person deletes their own message, with the agent's reply to it and the memories taken from it, while the message is younger than this many seconds.

admin.description: Admin access (ayni-spec D132 to D134, RBAC-ADMIN-001 to 008, RBAC-XSESS-009): a person whose roles hold auditor or operator opens Audit or Operations from the agent's card, after re-authenticating on the phone, for a grant of grantMinutes; and the internal admin interface, off unless enabled.

authentication.description: The re-authentication Show Admin asks on the phone (D127, IDENT-AUTH-015): an authenticate flow of purpose admin whose one combination is this set. Required whenever identity.roles declares auditor or operator (RBAC-ADMIN-002).

methods.description: The set of methods, by their names in identity.authentication.methods; it may hold confirming methods only (face-match, authenticator-app).

grantMinutes.description: How long an admin grant lasts, counted from the phone's confirmation and never moved by use; only a new confirmation opens a new one (RBAC-ADMIN-003).

internal.description: The internal admin interface, on a listener of its own inside the deployment (ADMIN_PORT, the loopback), opened only by the break-glass token ADMIN_TOKEN, each call recorded and flagged (D134, RBAC-XSESS-009).

enabled.description: false (default): no admin listener opens and ADMIN_TOKEN is read by nothing.

spaces.description: The rules of the Personal space and the templates of the spaces people may create (SPACE-DEF-002/003, ayni-agent decision 60).

personal.description: The rules of every Personal space (SPACE-DEF-002): 365 days, the lawful basis of the conversation-memory activity and the agent's provider by default; no handover.

creators.description: The roles of the people who may create a space from the template.

stewards.description: The roles of the stewards of the template's spaces, who name an owner of a space that has none, or on request (SPACE-MEMB-011).

membership.description: A list the owner keeps, or a rule with exactly one of department, group or organization: true; a template of kind organization has the rule organization: true.

rules.description: The default of each rule of a space and the bounds within which its owner may change it; a rule without bounds keeps its default.

allowedProviders.description: Provider names as llm.providerName gives them (llm.provider when it is absent).

features.description: The features the spaces of the template may use, in the order the clients show them (D120, TOOL-AVAIL-002), each with the providers it allows: sources of availability spaces that serve it.

default.description: The default provider: the only one when there is one; required with add: auto when there are several.

any.description: Whether the owner may let each member's own account reach any location in place of a list (TOOL-SPACE-014): for an entry one of whose providers has a personal account and serves a feature with a contract.

location.description: For Files: whether the agent makes and keeps the space's folder (managed), the owner picks one that exists (existing), or either (TOOL-FEAT-023). The managed mode is not built in this version.

availability.description: Where a source is available (TOOL-AVAIL-001): the whole agent, Personal only, or the spaces of the templates that name it as a provider of its feature.

featureId.description: The id of a feature (TOOL-FEAT-001): the key of tools.features, which a source's feature, a template's entries and the AG-UI profile name.

feature.description: One feature (D120, D121, TOOL-FEAT-001, TOOL-FEAT-005): the title people read; the profile of a feature with a contract; and, for a tool of that profile, its rule, step-up and approval bounds, set once for every provider.

tools.description: What the agent-pack says of a tool of the profile, for every provider: call, stepUp and approval only (TOOL-FEAT-005); its effect, title and trust are the profile's.

toolEffect.description: What a tool does (TOOL-CAT-006): it gives its default rule.

sourceAccount.description: Whose account a source's calls run with (TOOL-CAT-002): none, agent, space or personal (D104); organization is reserved for phase 3 and refused. A space account declares the fields its owner fills and the headers each call carries, built from them (D102); a personal account declares oauth, fields and apply, or from (TOOL-CAT-013).

fields.description: A space or personal account: the fields its owner, or the person, fills, one masked field each, in this order. Every field is a secret.

apply.description: A space or personal account: the headers of each call, {name} in a value standing for the value of that field.

oauth.description: A personal account of an MCP server: OAuth as MCP defines it, revision 2026-07-28 (D105, TOOL-CAT-014).

client.description: How the agent obtains its client at the authorization server: a client ID metadata document it serves, a client the operator registered (issuer, id and secret from the deployment's secrets), or Dynamic Client Registration. The agent never falls back from one to another.

scopes.description: The scopes asked; [] asks none. Absent: those of the server's challenge, else of its Protected Resource Metadata (TOOL-OAUTH-005).

bindingRequest.description: How the sign-in asks the service for the value of the account's binding (D110, layer a): a parameter of the authorization request, or a resource URL in which {value} stands for it.

from.description: A personal account: another source whose personal account this one uses, at the same URL (TOOL-CAT-015).

binding.description: A personal account: the binding of the source whose value each account is for (D110, TOOL-CAT-017).

check.description: A personal account: the read the agent makes once after each connection, outside the model, to name the account and check it (D110, TOOL-CAT-017). Each pointer is a JSON pointer (RFC 6901) into the tool's result.

tokenPatterns.description: A space or personal account: regular expressions that find a credential of the source in a message (D109, TOOL-CAT-016).

accountField.description: One field of a space account (D102): its name, unique in the account, what its owner is asked for, and the pattern its value must match.

accountHeader.description: A header each call of a space account carries (D102): every {name} of its value is replaced by the value of that field.

toolDeclaration.description: What the agent-pack says of one tool of a source (TOOL-CAT-001/006/007/008/010): its title, effect, rule, trust and step-up.

approval.description: The bounds and default of the tool's approval policy in a space, tighter than approvals.spaces (TOOL-CAT-023).

packApprovalPolicy.description: An approval policy of a tool of a space as the agent-pack writes it (INTX-APPR-020); it names no person and holds no timeout.

timeoutBounds.description: The default and the bounds, in minutes, of a kind of approval's timeout in a space (SPACE-DEF-008).

stepUp.description: A tool's step-up (D101, TOOL-CAT-010): the re-authentication, the auth challenge and the credential's freshness asked before the call, for this tool of this source only.

authentication.description: A re-authentication on the phone before the call (D127, IDENT-AUTH-015): an authenticate flow of purpose step-up asking the one set of enabled methods named here, which may hold confirming methods only (face-match, authenticator-app). Not asked again while an authentication of the person that held every method of the set completed within maxAgeMinutes.

maxCredentialAge.description: Seconds; 0 forces a fresh liveness check before each run; absent means the TTL N (D7).

authChallenge.description: The auth challenge a step-up asks before the call (D28, INTX-AUTH-002, TOOL-CAT-010): a device confirmation on the phone. An email code, a face match and a document read are asked as methods, in stepUp.authentication.

sourceId.description: The id of a source: the key of tools.sources, the name the AG-UI profile carries as `source`; an HTTP tool's id is also its tool's name (D101).

toolSource.description: One source of the tool catalog (D96, D101, TOOL-CAT-001): its type with its connection, what people read of it, whose account its calls run with, where it is available, who may use its tools (access) and what the agent-pack says of each of them (tools).

feature.description: The feature the source serves, a key of tools.features (D120, TOOL-FEAT-002): every MCP server and HTTP tool names one and is a provider of it; a bundled tool names none.

title.description: What people read on the cards, in the sources and in a space's settings; the source's id by default (TOOL-CAT-001).

access.description: The tier model of the source's tools (D12, D14, RBAC-TOOL); '*' names every tool of the source.

tools.description: What the agent-pack says of each tool of the source, by its name.

mcpSource.description: An MCP server (TOOL-MCP, D41): its connection, the tools it offers, the parameters it pins, its trust.

offer.description: The tools of the server the model is given; every tool it lists when absent (TOOL-CAT-003).

untrusted.description: What the source returns was written outside the organization (TOOL-CAT-008).

capabilities.description: A provider of a feature with a contract: the optional capabilities of its profile it uses at most; every one the server declares when absent (TOOL-FEAT-004).

manage.description: A provider of Files: the agent may make and keep a team space's folder at it (D145, TOOL-FEAT-023), with the space owner's own account (as: owner) or the managing account apply builds from the deployment's secrets (as: manager, D150). The managed mode is not built in this version: validated, and Files works in the existing mode.

httpSource.description: An HTTP tool (TOOL-HTTP-001): one tool, named by the source's id, and its request. `description` is what the model reads of the tool.

url.description: URL template; {param} placeholders are filled from parameters.

parameters.description: JSON Schema (object) of the tool's parameters as shown to the model.

untrusted.description: What the source returns was written outside the organization (TOOL-CAT-008).

bundledSource.description: A bundled tool (TOOL-HTTP-002): the one it names, on while the source is declared unless enabled is false. A bundled tool no source names keeps its default (statistics and generateImage off, the others on).

bundled.description: statistics, generateImage, principalCredentials, requestPresentation (request_presentation), credentialIssuance (credential_requirements and issue_credential), principalPreferences, workingMemory (MEM-TIER), connections (offer_connection: the Connect card of a person's own account, D108).

issuanceChallenge.description: The challenge of an issuance profile (INTX-ISSUE-010, architecture 11.5): a device confirmation, or the NFC read of a document. An email code and a face match are methods of the authentication (D126).

evidenceStore.description: The attributes of a piece of evidence whose values the agent keeps, sealed, and for how long (D67, PRIV-EVID-003). Omitted: no value is kept, only the audit fields.

days.description: Days the values are kept after the verification; kept until erased when absent.

onExpiry.description: archive: hidden from the model and the tools, readable by the auditor; erase: the key of the record is destroyed, its audit fields and digest remain.

evidenceModelVisible.description: The stored attributes the model may read (D67, D68). Omitted: none.

organizationMatch.description: One value, or a list of which any matches.

value.description: count: number of distinct approvers; percentage: 1 to 100 of eligible approvers.

toolAccess.description: The tier model of a source's tools, per (role, tool): ALLOW via roles, APPROVAL via approval, REQUESTABLE via elevation, DENY otherwise (D12, D14, RBAC-TOOL).

default.description: none: unlisted tools are denied; all: unlisted tools are allowed to every bound Principal.

roles.description: role -> tools in its ALLOW set. '*' allows every tool of the source.

approverConnectionType.description: Optionally restrict who may approve by connection type.

attested.description: The decision must be device-authenticated: an authorize flow on a flow-capable approver's wallet (INTX-APPR-011).

purposes.description: Ids from the top-level purposes list.
